newsitem.title: USA: Canola prices seen rising on Canada plantings data.
newsitem.headline: Canola prices seen rising on Canada plantings data.

text.p: Canola prices were expected to strengthen over the next few days following a bullish planting intentions report issued by Statistics Canada on Wednesday, Canadian analysts said.
StatsCan put Canadian canola area at 11.6 million acres, up 30 percent from last year but below most trade expectations which ranged from around 12.0 to 12.75 million.

"I still think we are going to see 12.5 million acres when its done but we're going to need higher prices to do that and I think the market is going to do that," said analyst Greg Kostal of Continental Grain Canada.
On the Winnipeg Commodity Exchange canola closed Tuesday at a premium of C$56.60 to flaxseed, basis the new crop November contracts.

Analysts said there were fewer surprises on cereals, although all wheat planting intentions were a little higher than some had anticipated at 28.8 million for all Canada and 28.2 million for western Canada.
A survey issued by UGG earlier this month projected all wheat plantings in western Canada at 27.393 million.
"Summer fallow acres were down and I think most were channeled into wheat," UGG's Jubinville said.
StatsCan projected summer fallow acres would fall by 5.3 percent to 14.1 million.
Barley acreage was slightly higher than expected at 12.7 million acres for all of Canada and 11.9 million for western Canada. The UGG survey had put western Canadian barley acreage at 11.83 million.
"We are well supplied on the feedgrain side of things now and another sizeable barley crop is eventually going to push us lower," UGG analyst Jubinville said of prices.
The report was also seen as bearish for oats, with acreage down four percent at 4.9 million but above expectations.
